name: 24-inch LED monitor (2017)
description: Fixed-height stand, full HD, PWM dimming that flickers at low brightness.

name: 24-inch efficient monitor
description: Flicker-free (DC dimming), height-adjustable stand, full HD, low power draw.

name: 27-inch QHD ergonomic monitor
description: Flicker-free, low-blue-light mode, height/tilt/swivel stand, sharper text (QHD), one USB-C cable to the laptop.

name: 34-inch ultrawide USB-C monitor
description: Curved ultrawide that replaces a dual-screen setup, flicker-free, fully adjustable, built-in USB-C dock; highest power draw.

name: Desktop tower PC (2019)
description: Fixed to the desk, audible fan; power management often disabled so many stay on after hours.

name: Laptop + docking station
description: Mobile (enables hot-desking and remote work), silent, aggressive sleep settings.

name: T5 fluorescent fixtures (2004)
description: 2x28 W tubes with electronic ballast, cool white, manual switches so lights stay on all day; maintenance is tube replacement.

name: LED tube retrofit
description: Drop-in LED tubes in the existing fixtures; no controls, same light distribution, flicker depends on driver quality.

name: LED panels + occupancy sensors
description: Flicker-free, neutral white (4000 K), good colour rendering (CRI>80); occupancy sensors switch off empty rooms and corridor sections.

name: Tunable-white LED + daylight and occupancy control
description: Flicker-free, high colour rendering (CRI>90), colour temperature follows the time of day (circadian), dims with daylight from facades and the atrium glass roof, occupancy sensing, individually dimmable.

name: Exterior manual lamella blinds (2004)
description: Cranked by hand; often lowered too late (overheating) or left down (lights on in daytime).

name: Motorised exterior blinds with sun sensors
description: Slats tilt automatically with the sun and retract in wind; blocks solar heat before it enters while keeping daylight and cutting glare.

name: Constant-volume air handling units (2004)
description: Fixed fan speed regardless of occupancy, plate heat recovery ~50%, F7 filters; near end of life.

name: EC fan retrofit + CO2 demand control
description: Keeps the existing units but swaps in efficient EC fans and adds CO2 sensors so airflow follows occupancy (keeps CO2 below ~1000 ppm); same capacity and heat recovery.

name: New AHUs with heat recovery + CO2 control
description: High-efficiency plate heat exchanger (~80%), CO2 demand control, F7 filters; sized 25% larger than today.

name: Premium AHUs: rotary heat recovery + CO2/humidity control
description: Rotary wheel recovers heat and moisture (~85%), keeps winter humidity at 40-60%, ePM1 filters remove most fine particles, very quiet; sized 50% larger than today.

name: Air-to-water heat pumps on the roof (2004)
description: Reversible outdoor units on the roof, buffer tanks and pumps in the basement plant room; efficiency has degraded with age and drops on cold days.

name: New air-to-water heat pumps
description: Modern variable-speed reversible units with natural refrigerant, quieter, better part-load efficiency; stays on the roof.

name: Lake-water heat pump (campus network)
description: Heat pump in the basement on a lake-water loop: stable source temperature all year, cooling mostly free from the lake; frees the roof for solar panels.

name: Server racks with room air conditioning
description: Research compute running 24/7, cooled by old room AC units; heat is dumped outside.

name: Consolidated servers + hot-aisle containment + free cooling
description: Virtualised, newer servers do the same work with less power; contained hot aisle and outside-air free cooling most of the year.

name: Open-frame FDM 3D printers (2019)
description: No enclosure, so ultrafine particles and fumes go straight into the room; heated bed often left on between prints.

name: Enclosed high-speed 3D printers with filtration
description: Enclosure with HEPA and carbon filter keeps particles and fumes out of the room, prints about twice as fast, switches off when done.

name: Bean-to-cup machine (2014), always warm
description: Keeps its boiler hot around the clock (no eco mode); decent coffee, frequent breakdowns.

name: Capsule machine pair
description: Two capsule machines: heat only on demand and switch off automatically, very little energy; cheap to buy but capsules cost 2-3x beans per cup and create waste; basic coffee, no fresh milk.

name: Office bean-to-cup machine with eco mode
description: Insulated boiler and eco timer; fresh beans and milk system, good quality, ~40 s per cup; maintenance is a service contract.

name: Dual-boiler espresso machine + grinder
description: Cafe-quality drinks and a social hub, but both boilers stay hot all day (high idle power), each drink takes ~1-2 min of staff time and it needs daily cleaning.

name: Central electric water heater + circulation loop (2004)
description: 1500 L tank kept at 60 C (legionella safety) with a loop to every WC and kitchen; the loop and tank lose ~10 kWh per day.

name: Heat-pump water heating
description: Hot water made by a heat pump (COP ~3) with a smaller, better insulated tank and loop.

name: No solar panels
description: Roof currently has no solar panels.

name: Rooftop solar panels
description: Monocrystalline panels on the roof around the atrium skylight; electricity used on site first, surplus sold to the grid.
